title: W9 closed-vacancy resume test asserts only absence of resume markers — empty 200 body passes
evidence:
resp.status |> should.equal(200)
  let body = simulate.read_body(resp)
  body
  |> string.contains("data-apply-page=\"form-resume\"")
  |> should.be_false
  body |> string.contains("draft-resume-banner") |> should.be_false
detail: The test name claims the closed page renders, but nothing asserts any closed-page content; a handler returning 200 with an empty body passes. Contrast resume_with_unknown_token_is_uniform_404_test, which asserts the "draft-not-found" body.
recommended_fix: Add a positive assertion for the closed page's marker (its data-apply-page value or heading copy) so the closed render itself is pinned, not just the resume page's absence.

title: W3 tombstone retains erased applicant's plaintext email as suppression key, pinned by test
evidence:
// Tombstone, not a hard delete: the row stays as the suppression record.
  draft_count(db) |> should.equal(1)
  draft_field(db, vacancy_id, "fields") |> should.equal("{}")
  draft_field(db, vacancy_id, "continue_token") |> should.equal("")
  draft_field(db, vacancy_id, "erased_at") |> should.not_equal("")
  draft_field(db, vacancy_id, "email") |> should.equal("tenant@example.com")
detail: The round-2 erasure fix keeps the erased applicant's readable email until vacancy close. An Art. 17 flow retaining plaintext PII as a suppression key weakens the erasure promise; a keyed hash satisfies the same (vacancy,email) re-save guard.
recommended_fix: Store HMAC(email, server secret) as the suppression key instead of the plaintext email; match incoming saves by hashing the submitted email.

title: Transfer-Encoding body-size rejection still tested POST-only after N20 fix
detail: The round-2 N20 fix added PUT arms for over-limit and missing Content-Length, but chunked Transfer-Encoding rejection is exercised only via http.Post. evaluate_body_size takes the method as an argument, so a method-conditioned TE arm would slip untested for the saver's PUT.
recommended_fix: Add an http.Put + Ok("chunked") case to the Transfer-Encoding rejection test.

title: Erasure GET confirm on a never-valid token unpinned; only replay-after-tombstone POST 404 covered
detail: Erasure 404 uniformity is pinned only by a replayed POST after tombstoning (status only, no body assertion). The GET confirm on a forged/never-valid token — what a bad erasure link hits — has no test, unlike resume's resume_with_unknown_token_is_uniform_404_test which also asserts "draft-not-found".
recommended_fix: Add forged-token tests for handle_erasure_confirm (GET) and handle_erasure_delete (POST) asserting 404 and the uniform not-found body.

title: seed_draft_with_token mints tok-seed via upsert then overwrites with a redundant UPDATE
detail: upsert_mints_the_token_at_save_time_test proves a fresh insert adopts the candidate token, so passing `token` to the upsert reaches the same end state in one statement. The UPDATE is redundant on the fresh databases every test runs against.
recommended_fix: Pass `token` as the upsert's candidate argument and delete the follow-up UPDATE statement.
